title: Identification and validation of three potential biomarkers and immune microenvironment for in severe asthma in microarray and single-cell datasets.
authors: Zhang, Fuying; Weng, Xiang; Zhu, Jiabao; Tang, Qin; Lei, Mingsheng; Zhou, Weimin
journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过微阵列和单细胞数据识别严重哮喘的生物标志物及免疫微环境，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Objective: The aim of this study was to identify genetic biomarkers and cellular communications associated with severe asthma in microarray data sets and single cell data sets. The potential gene expression levels were verified in a mouse model of asthma.Methods: We identified differentially expressed genes from the microarray datasets (GSE130499 and GSE63142) of severe asthma, and then constructed models to screen the most relevant biomarkers to severe asthma by machine learning algorithms (LASSO and SVM-RFE), with further validation of the results by GSE43696. Single-cell datasets (GSE193816 and GSE227744) were identified for potential biomarker-specific expression and intercellular communication. Finally, The expression levels of potential biomarkers were verified with a mouse model of asthma.Results: The 73 genes were differentially expressed between severe asthma and normal control. LASSO and SVM-RFE recognized three genes BCL3, DDIT4 and S100A14 as biomarkers of severe asthma and had good diagnostic effect. Among them, BCL3 transcript level was down-regulated in severe asthma, while S100A14 and DDIT4 transcript levels were up-regulated. The transcript levels of the three genes were confirmed in the mouse model. Infiltration of neutrophils and mast cells were found to be increased in severe asthma and may be associated with bronchial epithelial cells through BMP and NRG signalingConclusions: We identified three differentially expressed genes (BCL3, DDIT4 and S100A14) of diagnostic significance that may be involved in the development of severe asthma and these gene expressions could be serviced as biomarker of severe asthma and investigating the function roles could bring new insights into the underlying mechanisms.
abstract_zh: 目的：本研究旨在通过微阵列数据集和单细胞数据集，识别与重度哮喘相关的遗传生物标志物及细胞通讯，并在小鼠哮喘模型中验证潜在基因的表达水平。方法：我们从重度哮喘的微阵列数据集（GSE130499和GSE63142）中识别差异表达基因，然后通过机器学习算法（LASSO和SVM-RFE）构建模型筛选与重度哮喘最相关的生物标志物，并利用GSE43696进一步验证结果。单细胞数据集（GSE193816和GSE227744）用于识别潜在生物标志物的特异性表达及细胞间通讯。最后，在小鼠哮喘模型中验证潜在生物标志物的表达水平。结果：在重度哮喘与正常对照之间，共有73个基因差异表达。LASSO和SVM-RFE识别出三个基因BCL3、DDIT4和S100A14作为重度哮喘的生物标志物，并具有良好的诊断效果。其中，BCL3转录水平在重度哮喘中下调，而S100A14和DDIT4转录水平上调。这三个基因的转录水平在小鼠模型中得到确认。重度哮喘中观察到中性粒细胞和肥大细胞浸润增加，并可能通过BMP和NRG信号与支气管上皮细胞相关。结论：我们识别出三个具有诊断意义的差异表达基因（BCL3、DDIT4和S100A14），它们可能参与重度哮喘的发展，这些基因表达可作为重度哮喘的生物标志物，研究其功能作用可为潜在机制提供新见解。
